QUOTE: The high-level part is `ret & 0xFF80`, which names the module (e.g. CIPHER). ... The low-level part is `ret & ~0xFF80`. If it is zero, the high-level text stands alone. Otherwise, if the buffer already holds high-level text, it appends `" : "` ... or the joined form `HIGH : LOW`
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer describes the code's high-level module and low-level parts and says mbedtls_strerror joins them as "HIGH : LOW" when both are present.
